```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",

library(knowledge)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load}
# data from data-raw/vignette_method.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "knowledge", mustWork = TRUE)
x <- readRDS(vd("method.rds"))
pipe <- x$pipeline
reg <- x$settings
fun <- x$funnel
fsp <- x$funnel_species
ex <- x$examples
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v) paste0(format(round(100 * v, 1), nsmall = 1), " %")
fn <- function(stage) fun$n[fun$stage == stage]
issue <- function(n) {
  ifelse(is.na(n) | !nzchar(n), "",
         sprintf("[#%s](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/knowledge/issues/%s)", n, n))
}
# an SVG Graphviz wrote, inline and as wide as the column allows
svg_inline <- function(s) {
  s <- sub("^[^<]*(<\\?xml[^>]*>)?\\s*(<!DOCTYPE[^>]*>)?\\s*", "", s)
  s <- sub("<svg ", '<svg style="max-width:100%;height:auto" ', s, fixed = TRUE)
  htmltools::HTML(s)
}
scored <- fsp[fsp$stage == "scored", ]
stopifnot(fun$n[1] == 51587, nrow(scored) >= 1, all(diff(fun$n) <= 0))
lost_all <- fn("FDIS visits") - fn("no_link_segment")
lost_place <- fn("FDIS visits") - fn("ws50_mismatch")
stopifnot(lost_place / lost_all > 0.5)   # "most are lost to placement"
```

The thresholds this package recommends to link come from one pipeline: `r n0(fn("FDIS visits"))` electrofishing
visits from the Province's Fisheries Data Information System are placed on the BC Freshwater Atlas and on link's
segments, `r n0(fn("no_link_segment"))` of them are kept, and each species' rule is chosen by how well it predicts
where fish were caught in watershed groups it was not fitted to. This article walks the pipeline in order, one step
at a time: what each step does, the code that does it, how many records go in and come out, and every number that
shapes the result. Of the `r nrow(reg)` settings it lists, `r sum(reg$tested == "yes")` have been tested against an
alternative; the rest are the list of what to test next.

## What happens, in order?

Eleven steps, each done by one package. The box colour names the package.

```{r flow}
svg_inline(x$svg$flow)
```

## What feeds what?

Six sources reach the tuning: the FDIS export, the Freshwater Atlas, PCIC's modelled streamflow, the climate data and
Water Survey of Canada gauges wet's water balance is built from and fitted to, the province's other fish observations
(which shape link's segments but score no rule), and link's own configuration. The chart draws the first, second,
third and fifth as sources and folds the other two into wet's and link's boxes.

```{r lineage}
svg_inline(x$svg$lineage)
```

## Where are records lost?

A record that does not reach the tuning cannot inform it, so where the losses are matters as much as how many
remain. Most are lost to placement (`r pc(lost_place / lost_all)` of the `r n0(lost_all)` dropped): a visit whose
point lies far from any Atlas stream, or on a stream outside the watershed FDIS recorded, cannot be trusted to sit on
the stream that was fished.

```{r funnel, fig.height = 3, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Visits each step drops, in the order the steps run. Each bar is labelled with the count and the reason."}
f <- fun
f$drop <- c(NA, -diff(f$n))
f <- f[-1, ]
f$label <- factor(f$reason, levels = rev(f$reason))
ggplot(f, aes(x = drop, y = label)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n0(drop)), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 60, size = 3.2, colour = "#333333") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(v) format(v, big.mark = ","), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "visits dropped", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Of the `r n0(fn("FDIS visits"))` visits, `r n0(fn("no_link_segment"))` (`r pc(fn("no_link_segment") / fn("FDIS visits"))`)
remain on a link segment.

Each species then keeps only the visits its rules can speak to: on a stream line (not in a river polygon, a wetland
of 1 ha or more or a lake of 100 ha or more), of a usual fished area, in a group where link expects the species, with
no code that could hide it and no natural barrier to it downstream. The tests use the groups where the species was
caught at some visits and not others.

```{r funnel-species}
w <- stats::reshape(as.data.frame(fsp[, c("species_code", "stage", "n")]), idvar = "species_code",
                    timevar = "stage", direction = "wide")
names(w) <- sub("^n\\.", "", names(w))
gb <- unique(fsp[, c("species_code", "groups_both")])
w$groups <- gb$groups_both[match(w$species_code, gb$species_code)]
w[-1] <- lapply(w[-1], n0)
knitr::kable(w[, c("species_code", "kept", "stream_branch", "fished_area", "in_range", "not_blocked", "no_barrier",
                   "scored", "groups")],
             col.names = c("species", "kept", "stream line", "fished area", "in range", "not blocked",
                           "no barrier", "scored", "groups scored"),
             caption = "Rearing visits per species after each population filter. Scored visits lie in the groups with both outcomes.",
             align = "lrrrrrrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

## What does each step do?

Each block says what the step does, the code that does it, what goes in and comes out, and the settings it depends
on. A setting's row in the last section says where its value came from.

```{r steps, results = "asis"}
link_fn <- function(f) {
  if (grepl("^fwapg::", f)) {
    return(sprintf("[`%s`](https://smnorris.github.io/fwapg/03_functions.html#fwa-indexpoint)", sub("^fwapg::", "", f)))
  }
  sprintf("`%s()`", sub("^knowledge::", "", f))
}
counts <- list(
  `1` = sprintf("In: %s site visits, one row each.", n0(x$steps[["1"]][["visits"]])),
  `2` = sprintf(paste("In: %s visits. %s have a usable point and %s are placed on a stream within 500 m. %s are",
                      "dropped for lying more than 100 m from it and %s for lying outside the 1:50k tributary code",
                      "FDIS recorded; the check reaches only the %s placed visits that carry a full tributary code,",
                      "and %s of those disagree. Out: %s."),
                n0(fn("FDIS visits")), n0(fn("with a usable point")), n0(fn("placed on the Atlas")),
                n0(fn("placed on the Atlas") - fn("far_snap")), n0(fn("far_snap") - fn("ws50_mismatch")),
                n0(x$steps[["2"]][["ws50_checked"]]), n0(x$steps[["2"]][["ws50_mismatch_all"]]),
                n0(fn("ws50_mismatch"))),
  `4` = sprintf("Of the %s kept visits, %s (%s) take PCIC's routed flow and %s (%s) wet's water balance.",
                n0(x$steps[["5"]][["kept"]]), n0(x$steps[["5"]][["routed"]]),
                pc(x$steps[["5"]][["routed"]] / x$steps[["5"]][["kept"]]), n0(x$steps[["5"]][["balance"]]),
                pc(x$steps[["5"]][["balance"]] / x$steps[["5"]][["kept"]])),
  `5` = sprintf(paste("In: %s visits. Dropped: %s with no usable date, %s with no fished area or time, %s with an",
                      "unknown catch, %s with no link segment at their measure. Out: %s."),
                n0(fn("ws50_mismatch")), n0(fn("ws50_mismatch") - fn("junk_date")),
                n0(fn("junk_date") - fn("effort_sentinel_or_none")),
                n0(fn("effort_sentinel_or_none") - fn("catch_unknown")),
                n0(fn("catch_unknown") - fn("no_link_segment")), n0(fn("no_link_segment"))),
  `6` = paste0("Rules per species and stage: ",
               paste(sprintf("%s %s", sub("_", " ", names(x$steps[["6"]])), n0(x$steps[["6"]])), collapse = ", "),
               "."),
  `7` = paste0("Rules in the region (within one SE of the best): ",
               paste(sprintf("%s %s", sub("_", " ", names(x$steps[["7"]])), n0(x$steps[["7"]])), collapse = ", "),
               "."),
  `10` = sprintf(paste("On the Bulkley's %s segments, fresh's predicate passes %s for `default` and %s for the tuned",
                       "rule; the overlay and the connectivity pass then leave %s and %s."),
                 n0(ex$stages$segments), n0(ex$stages$pre_default), n0(ex$stages$pre_tuned),
                 n0(ex$stages$flag_default), n0(ex$stages$flag_tuned))
)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pipe))) {
  p <- pipe[i, ]
  fns <- strsplit(p$functions, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  cat(sprintf("### %d. %s\n\n%s\n\n", p$step, p$label, gsub("'", "’", p$does)))
  cat(sprintf("- **Run by:** %s; %s.\n", gsub(";", ", ", p$scripts), paste(vapply(fns, link_fn, ""), collapse = ", ")))
  esc <- function(v) gsub(">", "&gt;", gsub("<", "&lt;", v, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("- **In:** %s. **Out:** %s.\n", esc(p$inputs), esc(p$outputs)))
  if (!is.null(counts[[as.character(p$step)]])) cat(sprintf("- **Counts:** %s\n", counts[[as.character(p$step)]]))
  s <- reg[reg$step == p$step, ]
  if (nrow(s)) {
    cat("- **Settings:**\n")
    cat(sprintf("    - %s: %s%s\n", s$label, gsub(";", ", ", s$value),
                ifelse(nzchar(s$unit), paste0(" ", s$unit), "")), sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.na(p$issue) && nzchar(p$issue)) cat(sprintf("- **Open work:** %s\n", issue(p$issue)))
  cat("\n")
}
```

## How is a site placed?

A visit's point is snapped to the nearest Atlas stream within 500 m, and kept only if that stream is within 100 m.
The nearest stream is taken and the others in reach are not weighed; snapping among candidates is
[#91](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/knowledge/issues/91).

```{r snap}
row_of <- function(e, fate) {
  nb <- e$near
  data.frame(visit = e$site$site_visit, fate = fate, stream = nb$blue_line_key,
             name = ifelse(is.na(nb$gnis_name), "(unnamed)", nb$gnis_name), distance_m = nb$distance_m,
             chosen = ifelse(seq_len(nrow(nb)) == 1, "yes", ""))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(row_of(ex$kept, "kept"), row_of(ex$far, "dropped")),
             col.names = c("visit", "fate", "Atlas stream (blue line)", "name", "distance (m)", "snapped to"),
             caption = sprintf(paste("Two %s visits and every Atlas stream within 500 m of each. The first is kept;",
                                     "the second is placed, then dropped because its stream is more than 100 m away."),
                               ex$wsg),
             align = "llrlrl")
```

## What do the overlay and the connectivity pass change?

A rule is not the habitat link reports. fresh first applies the rule's test to each segment (the predicate); link's
hand-entered habitat reaches are then laid over it, and fresh's connectivity pass drops rearing with no spawning within
the bridge distance. On the Bulkley, the two later stages removed `r n0(ex$stages$dropped_default)` of the
`r n0(ex$stages$pre_default)` segments `default`'s predicate passed and `r n0(ex$stages$dropped_tuned)` of the
tuned rule's `r n0(ex$stages$pre_tuned)`, and added `r n0(ex$stages$added_default + ex$stages$added_tuned)`. That is why
the comparison regenerates both rules through all three stages rather than comparing a predicate with link's stored
flags.

## Which numbers shape the result, and which have been tested?

Every number below shapes a result: the pick, its stability checks, the grade or the comparison. Each was checked against the code and the run when this
article's data were written: a function's default, a script's constant, a literal in the code, link's configuration
at the comparison's commit (`r substr(x$meta$link_config_sha, 1, 7)`), or wet at the flow build the database held
(`r x$meta$wet_sha`). **Source** says where the value came from: a published source, a convention set here, a value
inherited from link or bcfishpass, or a value measured from data. **Tested** says whether the result has been
compared with another value. The untested rows come first: they are the work still to do.

```{r register}
r <- reg[order(reg$tested != "no", reg$source != "inherited", reg$step), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = r$label, value = gsub(";", ", ", r$value), unit = r$unit, step = r$step,
                        source = r$source, tested = r$tested, issue = issue(r$issue)),
             caption = "The settings register, from `inst/method/settings.csv`.", align = "llllllr")
```

## Software and citation

The pipeline runs on [`fwapg`](https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg) (the Freshwater Atlas in PostgreSQL, with New
Graph's [fork](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg) carrying PCIC's crosswalk),
[`link`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/link) (segments, access and habitat), [`wet`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet)
(flows), [`fresh`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fresh) (the habitat predicates and connectivity) and this
package, `knowledge`. This article's data were written on `r x$meta$written` at commit
`r x$meta$commit`, from the evidence ledger `r basename(x$meta$ledger)`.
